body:
Mostly matches the algorithm we used for etcpak (see the original PR #56931 )

I can't find where this code actually resizes the source image. If done correctly, the resize() call will indeed make certain pixel text blurry. I'm just not sure what can be done about it.

Here are the three ideas I see:

1. The PR as currently written: Smear the last 3 pixels on x and y instead of resizing could work, but the user would have to know this was done and adjust all their texture coordinates to (x / x + 3) which is really confusing. The fact that it will subtly break UVs is why I don't think we can do this.
2. Disallow compression of non-multiple of 4 textures
3. Allow overriding the size limitation (perhaps if the user targets Vulkan and not web)
4. What the etcpak PR did, resize the image which will look fine in most cases. (Usually we recommend not using VRAM compression on pixel art anyway).

There's no 100% perfect solution for VRAM compression. I think the way etcpak handled this is a reasonable compromise, and other engines do this too. If an artist wants full control, we should teach them to make their textures a multiple of 4 before compression.
LGTM, I tested it by randomly resizing and compressing `icon.svg` as S3TC serveral times and the resulting image looks correct
Looks good to me. It looks like the lower mipmap levels aren't always padded correctly, though that's also an issue with etcpak, so it doesn't block this PR from being merged
